tasks.description: Enforce rate limits using a token-bucket algorithm scoped to each API key. This will ensure each key gets an independent allowance. The algorithm should be able to handle a high volume of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when the token-bucket algorithm is applied, then the request is allowed or denied based on the available tokens.

tasks.description: Make the bucket capacity and refill rate configurable via application configuration. This should not require code changes to adjust them. The configuration should be stored in a central location.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid configuration, when the limits are updated, then the new limits are applied to the token-bucket algorithm.

tasks.description: Store rate-limit counters/state in Redis to enforce limits consistently across all server instances. This will ensure that the counters are shared across all instances.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made, then the counter is updated in Redis.

tasks.description: When a key exceeds its limit, reject the request with an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) status. This should include a Retry-After header indicating how long the client should wait before retrying.
acceptance_criteria: Given an API key that has exceeded its limit, when a request is made, then a 429 response is returned with a Retry-After header.

tasks.description: Write unit tests to ensure the rate-limiting middleware is working correctly. This should include tests for the token-bucket algorithm, configurable limits, and Redis-backed counters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when the rate-limiting middleware is tested, then the tests pass.

tasks.description: Integrate the rate-limiting middleware with the API routes. This should ensure that the rate-limiting is applied uniformly to all authenticated API traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made to an API route, then the rate-limiting middleware is applied.

tasks.description: Deploy the rate-limiting middleware to production. This should include configuring the Redis-backed counters and ensuring the middleware is applied uniformly to all API traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made to the production API, then the rate-limiting middleware is applied.
